pairs.question: Si manseritis in uerbo meo, uere discipuli mei estis. Quo fructu?
pairs.derivation: Augustine dramatizes the Lord's words (John 8:31-32) as a dialogue. The disciples' imagined question is 'Quo fructu?', framed by 'Et quasi quaererent,' (dropped) and 'secutus ait:' (dropped). The prior verbatim sentence 'Si manseritis in uerbo meo, uere discipuli mei estis.' is kept as setup so the question 'Quo fructu?' (to what benefit, sc. of remaining in the word) has a referent. Answer is the operative reply 'Et cognoscetis ueritatem.'; what follows is the next imagined question 'Quid prodest mortalibus ueritas?'.

pairs.question: Quid prodest mortalibus ueritas?
pairs.derivation: Second imagined exchange in the same dramatized dialogue. Question framed by 'Rursus quasi dicerent,' (dropped). Answer in source reads 'Et ueritas, inquit, liberabit uos.'; the speech tag 'inquit' is dropped as framing, leaving the contiguous reply 'Et ueritas liberabit uos.' What follows is Augustine's own gloss 'Vnde nisi a morte...', not part of the reply.
